answer: Ridge-Anchored Neighbor Overlap. Each agent's trust score is the edge count shared with its neighbors' neighbors, weighted by graph distance along the ridge separating clusters. A new identity entering through an umber cluster must reconstruct local links before gaining weight, and each synthetic edge adds measurable overlap cost. Replication requires rebuilding a distinct neighborhood per identity, so attack cost scales with the delta between cluster density and isolated-node density rather than a flat fee.
